classification.difficultyReason: Introduce the cylinder's half-height, use Pythagoras in an axial cross-section and substitute into the cylinder volume formula.

content.prompt:
A cylinder of radius $r$ cm is inscribed in a sphere of radius 8 cm.

Show that the volume of the cylinder is $$V=2\pi r^2\sqrt{64-r^2}.$$

spec.description: Unlabelled cylinder centrally inscribed in a sphere. The sphere outline and complete top elliptical rim are solid; the two cylinder sides and only the front arc of its bottom rim are drawn. Rim centres and elliptical flattening use a consistent orthographic projection, keeping the cylinder within the sphere outline.
spec.mathematics: An axial section gives a rectangle inscribed in a circle of radius 8 cm. The cylinder radius and half-height form the perpendicular legs of a right triangle with hypotenuse 8 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Question figure only; no radius, height or solution scaffold is added.

answer.short: With half-height $h$, $h=\sqrt{64-r^2}$, so $V=\pi r^2(2h)=2\pi r^2\sqrt{64-r^2}\text{ cm}^3$.
answer.worked:
Let the half-height of the cylinder be $h$ cm, so its full height is $2h$ cm.

In an axial cross-section, Pythagoras gives
$$\begin{align*}r^2+h^2&=64\\h&=\sqrt{64-r^2}.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}V&=\pi r^2(2h)\\V&=2\pi r^2\sqrt{64-r^2}\text{ cm}^3.\end{align*}$$
